Briefing for 13 November 2026

Short items for 13 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

New model

Gemini 4 Hydrogen is fast and now powers Google Search

Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast model for everyday coding and agent tasks at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens. It is the new default in AI Mode and is rolling out in the Gemini app and API.

Source: Google

Device

Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO

Nvidia says Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and board member, effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress leads as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.

Source: NVIDIA

In the background

Nonprofits sue five AI labs to pause new models

A coalition of advocacy groups filed suit in San Francisco against Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI, asking a court to halt new models over safety risks. The case has just been filed; no court has ruled.

Source: AP News

AI agents · More technical

OpenAI's new agents test and patch company code

OpenAI added Daybreak Red Team, which probes web apps for vulnerabilities in early access, and Daybreak Defense Factory, which finds and fixes flaws in codebases. Engineers review each proposed patch.

Source: The Register

AI agents

Mirendil raises $1 billion for agent-run AI research

Startup Mirendil closed a $1 billion Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake. It builds tools where hundreds of agents write code and run experiments, so small teams can do frontier AI research.

Source: Mirendil

In the background

OpenAI funds research on AI and children's safety

OpenAI signed a charter on safer AI for children at the Paris Peace Forum and pledged $2 million for shared research tools. It also says it wants to work with EU policymakers on the planned EU Kids Act.

Source: OpenAI

In the background

OpenAI's API can now run requests inside India

Eligible businesses can now have API requests processed and answered within India, starting with GPT-6 Luna. The goal is to meet local data rules, for example in financial services.

Source: The Hindu

Be brave. Get smart.
